writtenTo: The post-exilic community returning from Babylon
importantNotes: Chapters 1-9 contain extensive genealogies connecting the returned exiles to their ancestors.
Chronicles focuses on the positive aspects of David's reign (unlike Samuel/Kings).
David's preparations for the Temple highlight the importance of worship.
Written to encourage the post-exilic community about God's ongoing covenant.
David's prayer in chapter 29 is one of the most beautiful prayers of praise in Scripture.

chapters.1: Genealogy from Adam to Abraham and the descendants of Esau and Edom.
chapters.2: Genealogy of Jacob's sons, especially the line of Judah leading to David.
chapters.3: The descendants of David — the royal line.
chapters.4: Further genealogies of Judah and Simeon; Jabez's prayer.
chapters.5: Genealogies of Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
chapters.6: The descendants of Levi — priests, Levites, and their cities.
chapters.7: Genealogies of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, and Asher.
chapters.8: Genealogy of Benjamin, including King Saul's family.
chapters.9: Residents of Jerusalem after the exile; the Levitical gatekeepers.
chapters.10: The death of Saul and his sons in battle; the kingdom passes to David.
chapters.11: David is anointed king over all Israel; he captures Jerusalem; his mighty warriors.
chapters.12: Warriors who joined David at various points; support from all the tribes.
chapters.13: David's first attempt to bring the Ark to Jerusalem; Uzzah is struck dead.
chapters.14: David's family in Jerusalem; he defeats the Philistines twice.
chapters.15: The Ark is properly carried by the Levites and brought to Jerusalem.
chapters.16: David's psalm of thanksgiving; worship is organized before the Ark.
chapters.17: God's covenant with David — his house and throne will endure forever.
chapters.18: David's military victories and his just administration.
chapters.19: War against the Ammonites and Arameans.
chapters.20: Further victories over the Philistine giants.
chapters.21: David's census and its consequences; the threshing floor of Ornan is purchased.
chapters.22: David prepares materials and charges Solomon to build the Temple.
chapters.23: The organization of the Levites for Temple service.
chapters.24: The divisions of the priests descended from Aaron.
chapters.25: The musicians and singers organized for Temple worship.
chapters.26: The gatekeepers and treasurers of the Temple.
chapters.27: Military and civil leaders; David's officers and administrators.
chapters.28: David gives Solomon the plans for the Temple and charges him publicly.
chapters.29: Generous offerings for the Temple; David's prayer of praise; Solomon is crowned king.
